C-PLUGIN-PEAK-HOURS.IntentSummary: Add a pure provider-level peak-hours schedule library, a peak-hours server plugin that warns or blocks chat.message requests to peak-priced providers with dynamic off-peak connected-provider suggestions and session-age plus subagent grace, a persistent app_bottom TUI banner, conservative materialized revision-dated default schedules behind strict schema v3 validation, subpath and root package exports, README guidance, and synchronized GRACE graph, verification, and requirements projections.

MustPassCommand.Command: bun test src/lib/peak-hours.test.ts src/lib/plugin-toggle-config.test.ts src/lib/vvoc-config.test.ts src/plugins/peak-hours/index.test.ts src/tui/peak-hours/banner.test.ts

T-001.Title: Implement the pure provider-level peak-hours schedule library.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: src/lib/peak-hours.ts exports clock-injectable window types with start, end, explicit timezone defaulting to UTC, and an optional days restriction defaulting to all days, plus provider schedule records keyed by normalized provider id.

activeWindow evaluation handles same-day and cross-midnight windows, non-UTC timezones, weekday restrictions, and multiple windows per provider, returning the active window and its end boundary for until formatting.
Provider alias normalization maps known provider id spellings, at minimum deepseek, z-ai, zai, glm-family, qwen, and alibaba ids, onto schedule keys; unknown ids never resolve to a schedule.
Malformed windows fail open: parsing returns a warning and a no-schedule result and never throws from evaluation paths.
suggestion filtering takes connected provider ids plus schedules plus a clock and returns connected providers currently outside any active peak window.
Deterministic table-driven tests cover window math, midnight crossing, timezones, weekdays, aliases, fail-open parsing, suggestions, and message text building blocks with an injected clock only.
The module carries complete MODULE_CONTRACT, MODULE_MAP, block anchors, and LINKS referencing M-PEAK-HOURS-SCHEDULES.

T-002.Title: Extend plugin toggles, default schedules, materialization, and strict schema v3.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: plugin-toggle-config.ts adds the peak-hours toggle name, revision-dated DEFAULT_PEAK_HOURS_SCHEDULES for deepseek, z-ai, and qwen matching the approved 2026-08-21 windows, and materializePeakHoursEntry that expands boolean or missing entries to the full default and never overwrites user-provided mode, graceActiveSessions, or schedule values.

The embedded canonical schema in vvoc-config.ts gains a peak-hours arm accepting enabled, mode soft or hard, graceActiveSessions, and schedules with start, end, timezone, and optional days, rejecting malformed times, unknown modes, and unknown keys; every existing schema arm stays unchanged and schemas/vvoc/v3.json stays exactly equivalent.
Config parsing preserves peak-hours entries through createPluginToggleConfig and existing documents without the entry remain valid.
opencode.ts install, init, and sync paths materialize the peak-hours entry conservatively beside the existing hashline-edit and tool-history-compaction materialization calls.

Focused tests cover materialization conservatism for undefined, boolean, and user-edited object entries, schema acceptance and rejection cases, embedded and file schema equivalence, and sync behavior with injected fixtures.
Edited contracts, maps, change summaries, and block anchors remain accurate in every touched file.

T-003.Title: Implement the peak-hours server plugin with soft note, hard block, and grace.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: src/plugins/peak-hours/index.ts resolves the startup vvoc snapshot, honors the peak-hours toggle, and registers only the chat.message hook.
Soft mode appends a bounded system note naming the provider and window end when the message model's provider is in peak, without blocking processing.

Hard mode throws before any LLM request for non-grace messages, with error text naming the provider, window end, remaining wait, and dynamically suggested connected off-peak providers, degrading to suggestion-free text when all connected providers are peak-active.

Grace exempts sessions created before the active window start and sessions with parentID, derived from persisted session fields via SDK lookups, so decisions are identical after a simulated restart; internal agents compaction, title, and summary plus known subagent-like agents including guardian and mode subagent agents are never hard-blocked.
Suggestions enumerate connected providers through the config providers surface minus peak-active providers without additional credentials.
Schedule or provider resolution failures log a warning and degrade to soft or no-op, never to a block.
Hook-level deterministic tests with injectable clock, session lookups, and provider listings prove soft, hard, grace, exemption, suggestion, fail-open, and disabled-toggle no-hook cases.
The plugin carries complete MODULE_CONTRACT, MODULE_MAP, block anchors, and LINKS referencing M-PLUGIN-PEAK-HOURS.

T-004.Title: Implement the persistent app_bottom peak-hours TUI banner.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: src/tui/peak-hours/banner.tsx computes peak status from the shared schedule library, the effective vvoc config entry, the current model reference resolved from the open session's most recent model-bearing message with config model fallback, and api.state.provider for suggestions.

The banner registers in the app_bottom slot with a string plugin id, renders in warning colors while the current model's provider is in peak naming the provider, window end, and suggested off-peak providers, and returns nothing otherwise.
Registration is toggle-gated and fail-soft: a disabled entry or a failing slot API leaves the TUI untouched.
src/tui.tsx registers the banner beside the analytics indicator and branding footer with per-registration fail-soft isolation.

Deterministic tests with injectable clock, config, provider state, and model reference prove show and hide cases, suggestion text, toggle gating, and fail-soft registration without real OpenTUI rendering.
The banner module carries complete MODULE_CONTRACT, MODULE_MAP, block anchors, and LINKS referencing M-TUI-PEAK-HOURS-BANNER.

T-005.Title: Publish exports and document peak-hours behavior.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: src/index.ts re-exports PeakHoursPlugin and package.json adds the ./plugins/peak-hours subpath export with types and import targets matching existing plugin exports, plus the pack check script line importing the new subpath.

README documents the peak-hours plugin: purpose, hard and soft modes, global and per-provider mode override, grace semantics for active sessions and subagents, default schedule table with revision date and sources, alias normalization, dynamic connected-provider suggestions, the app_bottom banner, config examples, and the restart requirement.
README states that the plugin never substitutes models and never fetches pricing from the network.
Every documented command, path, field, and default is checked against current source and schema.

T-006.Title: Run the integrated regression gate and resolve only in-scope failures.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: All peak-hours, toggle, schema, opencode sync, plugin, and banner tests pass together with no live provider, credential, or real TUI dependency.
bun run check passes for the whole repository with no regressions outside the observed write scope.
No generated dist output, user OpenCode configuration, credential file, or unrelated plugin behavior is modified.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: The routed graph owns M-PEAK-HOURS-SCHEDULES, M-PLUGIN-PEAK-HOURS, and M-TUI-PEAK-HOURS-BANNER with accurate paths, purposes, dependencies, and verification links, and updates M-PLUGIN-TOGGLE-CONFIG, M-CLI-CONFIG, and M-PLUGIN-CONTEXT-TUI where behavior changed.
The verification projection owns V-M-PEAK-HOURS-SCHEDULES, V-M-PLUGIN-PEAK-HOURS, and V-M-TUI-PEAK-HOURS-BANNER with deterministic scenarios and commands, and updates the affected existing entries.
requirements.xml gains the peak-hours cost-governance goal and use case consistent with the approved specification.
Graph and verification indexes directly own every new anchor and current source LINKS fields match routed ownership.
bun run build, bun run pack:check, and bun run release:check pass with schema, package, and release metadata consistent.
GRACE lint and status report no errors attributable to C-PLUGIN-PEAK-HOURS, and git diff contains only approved files with no secrets or generated dist content.
